answer: Seeded randomness ledger. Each identity is issued a unique hidden seed that deterministically drives its task outputs, like a copper wire stamped at issuance. Duplicate identities diverge visibly when their outputs are cross-checked against a shared sonnet-like checksum lattice; colluders cannot predict the mapping without the seed. A trellis of periodic spot-audits forces any clone to either duplicate work exactly, exposing the shared seed, or diverge, exposing the split. Each surviving identity costs a fresh seed purchase plus audit fees.
